chapter: Portraits from Hemphill to Getz, and the bebop question
title: Why Benny Morton avoided the road
summary: Morton, a New Yorker attached to his mother, disliked one-nighters and stayed in demand for New York recording work.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: You mentioned -- you started to say that he didn't like traveling on the road, and then we sort of got away from it.
No, he stayed more or less with his

mother a lot. I don't think Benny ever married, in fact, unless it's been recently. He was single, but he just never liked the hazards of traveling. I think you can attribute that to the fact that the band -- the bands, I should say, that he joined, he heard learned so much that went on out there, that it didn't phase him at all.
He said, 'Well, I hope I'll never have to do this.' So I'm not surprised that -- if he went on the road with a few bands, he'd stay a week. That's a long time, boy, you know. for Benny Morton.

But when you're talking about months and months, and no way, and he was a typical New Yorker. He loved New York. He was brought up on the East Side, you know, and he talks that language, you know. He's just Benny Morton Martin, you know. He likes home. And I don't think that he's changed. I'd be willing to bet on that. He's one of the few that didn't care about the one nighters, one of those things, and he's always been in demand around New York. -- recording with the different bands and all that.
And that's another thing that's (Inaudible) kept him off of the road a lot.
